name: Chat panel
summary: A chat card with tabbed threads, header actions and a menu, assistant replies set in Markdown, and a prompt composer whose send adds your text to the open thread.

useWhen: Talking with an assistant in a few named threads beside your work
Showing assistant replies with light formatting and the trace line that led to each one
avoidWhen: Replies stream from a model or a server, which needs your own data layer
The conversation is the whole page rather than a panel

accessibility: The thread tabs are a Tabs list named Chats: arrow keys move between tabs, and the open thread follows the selected tab.
The open thread is the tab panel named by its tab, holding a log region, and the panel is a Tab stop that shows the Tabs focus ring.
The header actions are IconButtons named New chat and History, and a Menu trigger named More actions opens a menu named Chat actions.
The composer is a form: Enter sends, Shift plus Enter adds a line, and Send stays disabled until there is text.
Sending adds your text to the end of the open thread as a right-aligned message.
Assistant replies render through Markdown, which removes raw HTML and unsafe links, and each reply starts with a muted trace line.
unsupported: Sending to a model or a server: send only adds your text to the open thread
Streaming replies, attachments, or model choice
New chat, History, and the menu items: they do nothing until you add handlers
Scrolling a long thread: the thread grows with its messages
Keeping sent text: it resets on reload
workflowValue: Replaces wiring a chat card by hand: one tab value picks the thread, the composer draft and send run through one handler, and replies render as Markdown, so you swap the threads and keep the header, the thread, and the composer.
